bookingSettings.explicitCheckinSubHeading: Control whether specific roles must use the scanner-based explicit check-in flow instead of the one-click quick check-in. Only workspace owners can change this setting.
bookingSettings.countingOptionsSubHeading: Choose how kits are counted when visualising booking check-in/out progress.
bookingSettings.tagsRequirementSubHeading: Control whether users must add tags to their bookings. This helps with categorization and organization of bookings.
bookingSettings.automationSubHeading: Configure automatic actions for completed bookings to keep your workspace clean.
bookingSettings.timeRestrictionsSubHeading: Control booking timing constraints including minimum advance notice and maximum booking duration.
bookingSettings.workingHoursSubHeading: Manage your workspace's working hours. This will allow you to limit when bookings' start and end times and dates.
bookingSettings.requireTagsHint: When enabled, users must add at least one tag to their bookings. This helps with categorization and organization of bookings.
bookingSettings.explicitCheckinAdminHint: When enabled, administrators must use the scanner-based explicit check-in flow instead of the one-click quick check-in.
bookingSettings.explicitCheckinSelfServiceLabel: Require explicit check-in for Self Service
bookingSettings.explicitCheckinSelfServiceHint: When enabled, self-service users must use the scanner-based explicit check-in flow instead of the one-click quick check-in.
bookingSettings.ownerOnlySetting: Only the workspace owner can change this setting.
bookingSettings.countKitsAsUnitLabel: Count each kit as a single unit
bookingSettings.countKitsAsUnitHint: When visualising the state of a booking, treat each kit as one unit rather than counting the assets inside it.
bookingSettings.autoArchiveCompletedHint: Automatically move completed bookings to Archived after they've been completed for the specified number of days.
bookingSettings.autoArchiveExpiredLabel: Auto-archive reserved bookings after their end date
bookingSettings.autoArchiveExpiredHint: Automatically move reserved bookings to Archived once their end date has passed without ever being checked out — for teams that use bookings as a reservation calendar.
bookingSettings.autoArchiveDaysHint: Number of days to wait after a booking is completed (or its reservation's end date has passed) before automatically archiving it.
bookingSettings.minAdvanceNoticeHint: Users must book at least this many hours ahead of their booking start time. Enter 0 to allow immediate bookings. This limitation is only valid for <1>Self service</1> & <2>Base</2> users.
bookingSettings.maxBookingLengthHint: Set the maximum duration for a single booking. Leave empty for no limit. This helps prevent excessively long bookings.
bookingSettings.skipClosedDaysHint: Closed days will not be considered for calculations.
bookingSettings.notificationRecipientsSubHeading: The booking custodian always receives all notifications. These settings control who else gets notified. You can also add per-booking recipients when creating or editing a booking.
bookingSettings.notifyCreatorHint: When someone creates a booking on behalf of another person, the creator will receive all email updates for that booking.
bookingSettings.notifyAdminsLabel: Notify all admins on new booking requests
bookingSettings.notifyAdminsHint: When a booking is reserved, all workspace admins receive a notification so someone can review and handle the request. Admins will not receive subsequent updates (checkout, checkin, etc.) unless they are added as a notification recipient on the booking.
bookingSettings.alwaysNotifyHint: These users receive all booking email notifications for every booking in this workspace. Use this for people who need complete visibility, like an office manager or operations lead.

assetImport.title: Import assets
assetImport.updateForkText: <1>Want to update existing assets instead?</1> If you've exported assets from the Asset Index and made changes in Excel, you can re-import them to bulk update. <3>Go to bulk update →</3>
assetImport.createIntro: Upload a CSV file to create new assets. Start with our <1>CSV template</1> — each row becomes a new asset.
assetImport.warning: <1>IMPORTANT</1>: Do not use data exported from asset backup to import assets. You must use the template provided above or you will get corrupted data.
assetImport.baseRuleRelations: Columns like <1>kit, category, location & custodian</1> represent the name of the related entry — if it doesn't exist, we'll create it
assetImport.baseRuleTags: <1>Tags</1> can be comma-separated — missing tags will be created automatically
assetImport.baseRuleNewOnly: Each row creates a <1>new</1> asset — existing assets will not be merged or overwritten
assetImport.baseRuleQtyPointer: To onboard stock-room consumables (boxes, batteries, fasteners), or to link items to a reusable asset model, see <1>"Quantity-tracked assets"</1> below
assetImport.customFieldsIntro: Prefix your column heading with <1>"cf: "</1> and add the type after a comma. Supported types:
assetImport.qrIntro: You can link a QR code to each asset. This is useful if you already have QR codes printed and want to connect them to the assets you're importing. Limitations:
assetImport.qrRuleExisting: <1>Existing code</1> — the QR code must already exist in the system
assetImport.qrRuleNoDuplicates: <1>No duplicates</1> — each qrId must be unique per asset
assetImport.qrRuleNotLinked: <1>No linked codes</1> — the qrId must not already be linked to another asset or kit
assetImport.qrRuleOwnership: <1>QR ownership</1> — the code must be unclaimed or belong to your organization
assetImport.qrFallback: If no <1>"qrId"</1> is provided, a new QR code will be generated.
assetImport.barcodesIntro: Import assets with barcodes using these columns:
assetImport.barcodeCode128: <1>barcode_Code128</1> — 4-40 characters, supports letters, numbers, and symbols
assetImport.barcodeExternalQR: <1>barcode_ExternalQR</1> — 1-2048 characters (URLs, text, or any external QR content)
assetImport.barcodeRules: <1>Rules:</1> Use comma separation for multiple barcodes of the same type (e.g., "ABC123,DEF456"). Each value must be unique in your organization. Code39 and DataMatrix allow only letters and numbers; Code128 supports most symbols. Values are automatically converted to uppercase. Leave barcode columns empty if you don't want to assign barcodes.
assetImport.qtyIntro: Six optional columns let you onboard stock-room consumables (boxes, batteries, fasteners) and link individually-tracked assets to a reusable asset model:
assetImport.qtyColType: <1>type</1> — <3>INDIVIDUAL</3> (the default if the column is missing or the cell is blank) or <5>QUANTITY_TRACKED</5>. On <7>update</7> imports, the cell is silently ignored — type cannot be changed once an asset exists.
assetImport.qtyColQuantity: <1>quantity</1> — required, must be a positive integer when <3>type = QUANTITY_TRACKED</3>. Ignored on <5>INDIVIDUAL</5> rows.
assetImport.qtyColMinQuantity: <1>minQuantity</1> — optional non-negative integer; sets the low-stock alert threshold. Ignored on <3>INDIVIDUAL</3> rows.
assetImport.qtyColUnitOfMeasure: <1>unitOfMeasure</1> — optional free-text label (e.g. <3>boxes</3>, <5>liters</5>, <7>kg</7>). Markdoc injection characters are stripped.
assetImport.qtyColConsumptionType: <1>consumptionType</1> — required when <3>type = QUANTITY_TRACKED</3>. <5>ONE_WAY</5> (consumed on checkout, no return) or <7>TWO_WAY</7> (returned with a consumption report). Ignored on <9>INDIVIDUAL</9> rows.
assetImport.qtyColAssetModel: <1>assetModel</1> — optional asset model name; created automatically (case-insensitive lookup) if it doesn't exist yet. <3>INDIVIDUAL rows only</3> — on a <5>QUANTITY_TRACKED</5> row during update, the cell is skipped with a warning and the rest of the row still applies.
assetImport.qtyTip: <1>Tip:</1> the downloaded template above already contains one <3>INDIVIDUAL</3> example with an <5>assetModel</5> and one <7>QUANTITY_TRACKED</7> example with <9>quantity</9> and <11>consumptionType</11> filled in.

assetUpdate.title: Update existing assets
assetUpdate.intro: Edit your assets in Excel or Google Sheets, then upload the CSV here. We'll show you exactly what will change before anything is saved.
assetUpdate.step1: <1>Step 1:</1> Go to the <3>Asset Index</3>, select the assets you want to update, and export them. Make sure your export includes the <5>Asset ID</5> or <7>ID</7> column so we can match rows to existing assets.
assetUpdate.whatYouCanUpdateBody: Name, Category, Location, Tags, Valuation, Available to book, and your custom fields (Text, Boolean, Date, Option, Number, Currency).
assetUpdate.notSupported: <1>Not supported yet:</1> Description, Status, Kit, and Custody can't be bulk-updated via CSV — Status and Custody have their own workflows, and Description can lose formatting during export. These columns will be safely skipped if present in your file.
assetUpdate.emptyCellsClearBody: If a field currently has a value and you leave the cell empty, that value will be cleared. Fields that are already empty stay unchanged. Name and boolean fields (Yes/No) cannot be cleared.
assetUpdate.howMatchedBody: By <1>Asset ID</1> or <3>ID</3> — keep these columns as they are. Categories, locations, and tags that don't exist yet will be created for you.
assetUpdate.limitsBody: You can update up to <1>1,000 assets</1> per file. For larger batches, split your CSV into multiple files.
assetUpdate.tip: <1>Tip:</1> Just need to change one field on many assets? Select them in the <3>Asset Index</3> and use <5>Actions</5> — no CSV needed.
